images.caption:
Photo taken at the Vardøhus Fortress on the outskirts of Vardø town in Finnmark, Norway:
Weather-beaten wooden direction sign on a post, with "Jan Mayen 790 nautical miles" engraved, located by the coastal fortress. Jan Mayen is a Norwegian volcanic island in the Arctic Ocean with no permanent population.
Vardøhus Fortress (Norwegian: Vardøhus festning) is located in the town of Vardø in Troms og Finnmark county, Norway, on the island of Vardøya on the Barents Sea near the Russian border. The northernmost fortress in the world was originally built around 1307 as a defense against raids from people further east and to secure Norwegian dominion of Finnmark and the northern territories. The current Vardøhus Fortress was constructed between 1734 and 1738 and remains largely intact in its original form to this day. Covering an area of 25 acres, the defense facility is designed as an octagonal star with low stone-clad earth ramparts. Inside the fortification walls, there are nine distinctive buildings.

images.filename: VARDØ Vardøya NORWAY Steilneset minnested Heksemonument hekser (Witches’ Memorial 91 victims 17c Finnmark) Louise Bourgeois fire sculpture Peter Zumthor Glass pavillion 145 m Hall corridor (2011) Fog Bussefjorden Distorted pano 2023.jpg
images.caption:
Steilneset Memorial (The Witch Monument or Witch-hunt memorial at Steilneset) is located just off the town of Vardø, by the Barents Sea in the easternmost part of Finnmark, Norway. 
The monument opened in 2011 in memory of the 91 victims of the witch trials and executions in Finnmark from 1600 to 1692, most of whom were burned at the stake at Steilneset. The memorial is part of the National Tourist Routes and consists of:
The "Flame House" featuring the installation The Damned, the Possessed and the Beloved by the French-American artist Louise Bourgeois (1911–2010), which includes a chair with flames in the seat and seven large oval mirrors.
A 135-meter-long memorial hall made of sailcloth that houses a dark corridor with simple light bulbs and biographies (memorial plaques) of the victims written by Professor Liv Helene Willumsen; the Glass Pavilion for the artwork and the promenade hall were designed by Swiss architect Peter Zumthor (born 1943).
Distorted panoramic photo taken at the end of July with fog over Vardøya and Bussesundet towards the mainland in the west.
